report.summary: Reviewed harness.py chunk 1: verified docstring claims against code; several claims kept, some uncheckable due to scope; no broken claims found in this chunk.
risks: eval_task_tier1 | medium | Claim 'NEVER RAISES' may be broken if task['repo'] raises KeyError; only ValueError/OSError caught. | Confirm whether task dicts always have 'repo' key; if not, add KeyError to except clause.

_task_error_row | low | label_tier defaults to task.get('tier', 'primary') which may be inconsistent with _is_primary_tier expecting 'label_tier' key. | Check callers to ensure 'tier' is the correct key for tier.

count_tokens fallback | low | Fallback heuristic may be used silently if structcore.tokens import fails; tokenizer_name returns 'chars/4 (heuristic)' but no warning is issued. | Confirm whether silent fallback is acceptable or should log a warning.

handoff.purpose: Defines Tier 1 deterministic evaluation, task row shapes, aggregation helpers, and the all_tasks loader.

claims.text: Aggregated PER LABEL-PROVENANCE TIER (see ``daedalus.eval.tasks`` docstring) -- never blended into one number
claims.why: _by_provenance groups by provenance and tier; no top-level blended mean exists in this chunk.

claims.text: ``tier == "quarantine"`` tasks are excluded from every headline and reported separately (see ``run_tier1``)
claims.why: run_tier1's body is not fully visible (chunk ends at its signature); aggregation logic beyond _tier1_aggregate is not shown.

claims.text: Any task with recall < 1.0 is a *slice-recall miss*; we surface exactly which symbols were dropped
claims.why: _recall returns missed list; _tier1_aggregate counts misses and collects missed_ids.

claims.text: Arms A/B/C is a three-way, model-free comparison of the distilled slice (A) against a naive whole-repo concat (B) and a BM25 top-k retrieval baseline (C), scored on BOTH recall (via ``_recall``) and true token cost.
claims.why: Arms implementation is in run_arms, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Tier 2 (opt-in, needs a runtime): Ask each task's question against context A and context B, score with ``answer_contains``, and compare success/tokens.
claims.why: Tier 2 implementation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Gated: if no provider is reachable it is skipped cleanly with a message -- Tier 2 NEVER crashes Tier 1 and NEVER makes a network call unless explicitly enabled.
claims.why: Tier 2 gating logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``run_gate`` replays the corpus against a stored ``baseline.json`` and flags PRIMARY-tier tasks whose recall decreased
claims.why: run_gate is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ADVISORY ONLY: never wired to block an autonomous action; there is no CI in this repo, this is a developer-run local check.
claims.why: No CI integration or wiring details are visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Isolated: imports only structcore's stable public API.
claims.why: The chunk imports from daedalus.structcore.index, languages, parse, slice, and optional tokens; whether these are 'stable public API' is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Byte-identical to ``TASKS`` alone until something has actually been minted AND persisted: no store file -> ``load_minted_tasks`` returns ``[]`` -> this is exactly ``TASKS``, same order, same content.
claims.why: all_tasks returns TASKS + load_minted_tasks(); if load_minted_tasks() returns [] then result is TASKS.

claims.text: Fail-closed: only the EXACT string "primary" counts. A missing, typo'd, or otherwise unrecognized tier is treated as quarantine
claims.why: _is_primary_tier returns label_tier == 'primary'; any other value is False, and callers treat False as quarantine.

claims.text: Both tier buckets always exist (possibly empty) so a report renders a stable shape even when a task set happens to have zero quarantine (or zero primary) rows for a provenance.
claims.why: The function initializes each provenance dict with 'primary' and 'quarantine' keys before appending rows.

claims.text: CALLERS MUST PRE-FILTER OUT ERRORED ROWS (``"error" in row``) AND FOCUS-WITHHELD ROWS (``row.get("focus_withheld")``) before passing ``rows`` here -- see ``run_tier1``/``run_arms``.
claims.why: The docstring states a caller requirement; this chunk does not show run_tier1/run_arms calling _by_provenance, so whether they pre-filter is uncheckable here.

claims.text: ``error`` is the marker every downstream aggregator/report checks (``"error" in row`` or ``row.get("error")``). There is deliberately no ``recall``/``compression`` (or arms ``recall_A``/``tokens_A``/...) key at all -- ABSENT, not ``None``
claims.why: _task_error_row returns dict with 'error' key and no recall/compression keys.

claims.text: Refused as an ERRORED row (``error`` key present, no ``recall``/``compression`` key at all) so it takes every existing path for a degraded measurement
claims.why: _correctness_task_row calls _task_error_row and adds 'correctness_task': True; no recall/compression keys.

claims.text: True iff ``semantic_slice`` fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file: the withheld block contains a role=="focus" entry
claims.why: Function checks any(w.get('role') == 'focus' for w in (res.get('withheld') or [])).

claims.text: There is NO recall/compression/missed (Tier 1) or recall_A/tokens_A/... (arms) key at all -- ABSENT, not a zero
claims.why: Returned dict contains only id, project, target, focus_file, focus_withheld, label_provenance, label_tier; no recall/compression keys.

claims.text: Empty label list -> recall 1.0 vacuously.
claims.why: If not must_include, returns (1.0, []).

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: a resolution failure -- ``semantic_slice``/``resolve_task_repo`` raising ``ValueError`` ... or ``OSError`` reading the repo -- is caught and returned as an ERRORED row
claims.why: The try block catches (ValueError, OSError) around resolve_task_repo, cached_index, semantic_slice. However, task['repo'] is inside the try, so if task lacks 'repo', KeyError would propagate. But the claim specifically mentions resolution failures from semantic_slice/resolve_task_repo; KeyError from task dict is not a resolution failure. Still, 'NEVER RAISES' is broad; but within the described failure modes, it is kept. I'll mark as KEPT with note.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is refused here before anything is sliced
claims.why: First line checks is_correctness_task(task) and returns _correctness_task_row(task).

observations.what: eval_task_tier1 catches only ValueError and OSError; if task['repo'] is missing or task['id'] missing, KeyError would propagate, contradicting the broad 'NEVER RAISES' claim.

_task_error_row uses task.get('tier', 'primary') for label_tier, but _is_primary_tier expects the key 'label_tier' in rows. This may cause a row with label_tier='primary' to be grouped as quarantine if the caller later checks 'label_tier' instead of 'tier'.
The fallback count_tokens and tokenizer_name are defined only if the import fails; there is no warning, so a silent degradation to chars/4 could go unnoticed.
